events.scenario_brief: Danielle, her spouse, and their 14-year-old daughter are planning a six-night San Diego trip during summer break. They can depart Dallas on Saturday or Sunday, and they want time for beach days, a harbor activity, and one scheduled youth-arts program. Nonstop fares vary sharply by departure day, while hotels in Mission Bay, Coronado, and downtown differ in room layouts for three people, resort charges, parking costs, and travel time to the planned activities.

events.continuity_hook: The vacation dates are fixed, but Danielle needs the flight times and ticket total settled before confirming which hotel location best fits arrival and departure.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the viable flight pairings by total cost for three travelers, baggage charges, ticket terms, airport timing, and vacation time, then select the itinerary that fits the scheduled activities.
events.scenario_brief: The family has decided to travel Saturday through Friday and is comparing two outbound nonstops and three returns. The least expensive outbound arrives late enough to eliminate most of the first day, while the earlier flight costs more but allows hotel check-in before the evening harbor reservation. The return choices differ in fare, checked-bag charges, and how early the family would need to leave the coast.

events.continuity_hook: Flights are selected for the six-night stay, leaving the hotel, airport transfers, and daily transportation plan to be finalized.
events.interaction_goal: Verify that each room accommodates three guests, calculate six-night totals with taxes and required charges, compare transportation costs and cancellation terms, and reserve the property that best fits the family itinerary.
events.scenario_brief: With an early Saturday arrival and an afternoon Friday return selected, Danielle is comparing a Mission Bay resort with a downtown hotel. The resort has direct beach access and a larger two-bed room but adds a daily resort charge and higher parking; the downtown property has a lower room rate and breakfast for three but would require daily travel to the beach. Both offer refundable rates, though their deposit dates and cancellation deadlines differ.

events.continuity_hook: Flights and lodging are booked, but the room reassignment could affect sleeping arrangements, unpacking, and the first full beach day.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm occupancy and rollaway details, compare the total added cost and inconvenience of both remedies, secure an acceptable room arrangement, and update the first-morning schedule if a room move is required.
events.scenario_brief: The reserved Mission Bay resort has notified Danielle that the original two-bed room will be unavailable for the first night because of maintenance. It can provide a king room with a rollaway for one night and move the family the next morning, or transfer the entire stay to a larger room in another building for an added nightly amount. The resort will keep the original cancellation deadline while Danielle decides.

events.continuity_hook: The forum schedule is known, but Danielle has not decided whether to attend the dinner or selected flights, hotel nights, or a complete reimbursable itinerary.
events.interaction_goal: Compare one-night and two-night itineraries, account for meeting and dinner timing, calculate airfare, lodging, and local transportation totals, and identify options within the organization's trip allowance.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle needs to attend a regional partner forum in Denver with a Thursday afternoon planning meeting, a Friday program, and an optional Friday evening dinner. She can fly from Dallas on Thursday morning or Wednesday evening, and either return late Friday or stay until Saturday morning. The venue hotel has a meeting rate for one or two nights, while less expensive properties near Union Station would add local transportation.

events.continuity_hook: The trip will run Thursday through Saturday and the venue room rate is still available, but flight selection must be completed before the hotel dates and airport transfers are booked.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the remaining flight combinations by total fare, baggage terms, meeting margin, Saturday departure logistics, and Dallas arrival time, then choose the itinerary that accommodates the full forum program.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle has confirmed that the Friday dinner is important and will stay until Saturday. The outbound search now centers on a Thursday morning nonstop with a workable meeting margin and a cheaper flight that arrives only shortly before the session. Two Saturday returns differ in fare, carry-on rules, and whether she would need to leave the hotel before breakfast service begins.

events.continuity_hook: The full forum schedule and flights are fixed; lodging and airport transportation are the remaining unbooked portions.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate comparable two-night totals, verify payment and cancellation terms, account for local transportation and Saturday luggage storage, and reserve the option that fits the trip allowance.
events.scenario_brief: With Thursday-morning and Saturday-afternoon nonstops selected, Danielle needs two Denver hotel nights. The venue hotel still offers the forum rate and eliminates daily meeting travel, while a Union Station property has a lower base rate but adds rail or rideshare trips and an earlier cancellation deadline. Breakfast hours, required fees, and Saturday luggage storage must be included in the comparison.

events.continuity_hook: All reservations remain in place; only the Friday transition from the forum to dinner and the resulting reimbursable transportation estimate need attention.
events.interaction_goal: Map a workable post-session departure time, compare rail-plus-walk and rideshare timing, confirm the return trip to the hotel, and update the local transportation estimate.
events.scenario_brief: The forum organizer has moved Friday evening's dinner from the venue hotel to a restaurant in RiNo and set an earlier start time. Danielle's hotel and flights remain confirmed, but the revised location leaves little time after the final program session and alters her evening transportation plan.

events.continuity_hook: The summit sessions are fixed, but arrival day, return day, flights, hotel nights, and the complete reimbursable estimate are unresolved.
events.interaction_goal: Build realistic one-night, two-night, and three-night itinerary combinations, compare meeting margins and total costs, and narrow the trip to a practical schedule.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle will represent the nonprofit at an Atlanta sponsor summit with a Monday afternoon roundtable and a Tuesday morning presentation. She can leave Dallas early Monday or travel Sunday evening, and Tuesday offers either an evening nonstop or a less expensive Wednesday-morning return. Hotels near the Midtown venue vary in nightly cost, breakfast availability, and access from the airport.

events.continuity_hook: Sunday arrival is settled, but the exact outbound and return pairing must be chosen before hotel dates can be confirmed.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the remaining flight pairings by airfare, baggage terms, airport timing, hotel-night impact, and Dallas arrival time, then select the itinerary that protects both summit sessions.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle has ruled out arriving Monday because the available nonstops leave too little recovery time before the roundtable. Two Sunday-evening departures now differ in fare and arrival time, while Tuesday-evening and Wednesday-morning returns differ in ticket terms, baggage charges, and whether another hotel night is necessary.

events.continuity_hook: Flights are selected for Sunday through Tuesday; lodging and airport transfers are the only outstanding trip components.
events.interaction_goal: Compare two-night totals with taxes and required fees, verify breakfast and luggage arrangements, review payment and cancellation terms, and reserve the better overall option.
events.scenario_brief: After selecting a Sunday-evening arrival and Tuesday-evening return, Danielle needs two hotel nights in Midtown. The summit hotel has a higher flexible rate and direct indoor access to the meeting rooms, while a nearby property costs less and includes breakfast but requires an outdoor walk and has a prepaid booking deadline. Both can hold luggage after Tuesday checkout.

events.continuity_hook: The Atlanta trip remains booked, but the outbound schedule must be resolved while the airline's alternate-flight offer is available.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the revised arrival times, total ticket and baggage costs, hotel check-in timing, and Monday readiness, then secure the most practical outbound option and refresh the airport-transfer plan.
events.scenario_brief: The airline has retimed Danielle's Sunday flight to arrive nearly two hours later, leaving a very late hotel arrival before Monday's roundtable. She can accept the new schedule, move to an earlier nonstop at no added fare, or take a slightly later departure on another airline that requires paying for a carry-on. Her Tuesday return and hotel reservation are unaffected.

events.continuity_hook: The meeting schedule is confirmed, but travel dates, flights, hotel nights, airport transportation, and the reimbursable total remain unresolved.
events.interaction_goal: Compare practical Tuesday-through-Thursday and Tuesday-through-Friday itineraries, including airfare, one or two hotel nights, airport transfers, meeting margins, and total trip cost, then narrow the trip to a workable schedule.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle is scheduled for a Wednesday afternoon partner roundtable and a Thursday morning site visit in Chicago. She can leave Dallas Tuesday evening or Wednesday morning, then return Thursday evening or Friday morning. The convening hotel in River North has a limited group rate, while two nearby hotels have lower advertised prices but different fee, breakfast, and cancellation terms.

events.continuity_hook: The trip will require two hotel nights, but the exact flight pairing must be selected before she can finalize lodging and transfer times.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the remaining flight combinations by full ticket cost, baggage terms, Tuesday hotel arrival, Thursday airport margin, and Dallas arrival time, then select the pairing that fits the convening schedule.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle has chosen to travel Tuesday evening and return Thursday after the site visit. Two outbound nonstops differ in fare and arrival time, while the viable Thursday returns differ in ticket restrictions, carry-on charges, and the amount of time available to reach the airport after the visit.

events.continuity_hook: Flights and meeting times are fixed; the hotel and airport-transfer plan are the final unbooked parts of the Chicago trip.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate comparable two-night totals with taxes and mandatory charges, verify cancellation and luggage-storage terms, include airport transportation, and reserve the option that fits the approved trip amount.
events.scenario_brief: With Tuesday-evening and Thursday-evening flights selected, Danielle needs two nights in River North. The convening hotel offers direct access to Wednesday's roundtable but charges a destination fee, while a nearby hotel includes breakfast and has a lower nightly rate but requires a morning walk and has an earlier cancellation deadline. Both will store luggage after Thursday checkout.

events.continuity_hook: The family dates and main activities are known, but transportation, lodging area, room configuration, parking, and the overall trip budget still need to be worked out.
events.interaction_goal: Compare flying and driving door to door, estimate transportation and parking costs, evaluate one-hotel and split-stay structures, and identify the most practical framework for the five-night trip.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle, her spouse, and their daughter are planning a five-night spring-break trip to St. Louis built around Forest Park museums, a scheduled evening performance, and one day in the central corridor. They are weighing a short flight from Dallas against driving, and they have not decided whether to stay near Forest Park for the entire visit or split the stay with downtown.

events.continuity_hook: Driving dates and the single-hotel plan are settled; choosing and reserving lodging will determine the trip's fixed cost and daily driving pattern.
events.interaction_goal: Verify occupancy and bedding, calculate five-night totals with taxes and parking, compare breakfast value and cancellation terms, and reserve the hotel that best fits the planned activities.
events.scenario_brief: The family has decided to drive and use one hotel for all five nights. Danielle is comparing a suite-style property near Forest Park with separate sleeping space and breakfast against a less expensive central-corridor hotel offering two beds, paid parking, and a shorter cancellation window. Each option states that it can accommodate three guests, but taxes, parking charges, deposit timing, and the exact bedding need verification.

events.continuity_hook: The road-trip schedule and hotel reservation remain in place, but the room change must be resolved before the cancellation deadline and before the family commits to the final lodging cost.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm the studio and suite bedding layouts, calculate the discounted and upgraded five-night totals, compare the practical impact of each arrangement, and retain, modify, or replace the reservation before the deadline.
events.scenario_brief: The reserved Forest Park-area hotel has changed the family's assigned room from a one-bedroom suite to an open studio with the same occupancy limit. It can restore a separate-bedroom layout at a higher nightly price or keep the studio and provide a partial rate reduction. The original cancellation deadline is three days away, and the family has not yet decided whether the revised sleeping arrangement is acceptable for five nights.

events.continuity_hook: The family is still driving to St. Louis on the planned dates; only the final lodging arrangement and its fixed cost remain unsettled.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the three available room arrangements, bedding, parking, taxes, and payment terms, then modify or replace the reservation before the deadline.
events.scenario_brief: With the cancellation deadline now one day away, Danielle has confirmed that the discounted studio has two queen beds but no door between the sleeping and sitting areas. The hotel can instead restore a one-bedroom suite with one king bed and a sofa bed for a higher five-night total, while a comparable nearby property still has a two-room suite available with paid parking.

events.continuity_hook: The meeting times are fixed, but travel dates, flight timing, lodging, ground transportation, and the reimbursable total have not been selected.
events.interaction_goal: Build workable Monday-through-Wednesday and Tuesday-through-Wednesday itineraries, compare total costs and meeting margins, and choose the trip structure to take forward.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle needs to attend a Tuesday afternoon foundation meeting and a Wednesday morning corporate-partner breakfast in Boston. She can fly from Dallas Monday evening or very early Tuesday, and the usable returns leave Wednesday afternoon or evening. Hotel candidates near Back Bay differ in total price, walking distance to the meetings, and whether Tuesday-morning arrival would require luggage storage before check-in.

events.continuity_hook: The trip dates and two-night stay are settled, but the exact flight pair must be chosen before the hotel and Wednesday schedule can be finalized.
events.interaction_goal: Compare complete airfare and baggage costs, Monday hotel-arrival timing, Wednesday airport margins, and ticket terms, then select and book the practical flight pair.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle has chosen a Monday-evening departure and Wednesday-evening return. Two outbound nonstops differ in fare and Boston arrival time, while the return choices differ in carry-on charges, change terms, and how much time they leave after the Wednesday breakfast for an additional office visit.

events.continuity_hook: Air travel and meeting times are fixed; lodging and airport transfers are the remaining trip components.
events.interaction_goal: Verify room availability, mandatory charges, breakfast terms, cancellation timing, and luggage storage; calculate comparable two-night totals and reserve the better fit.
events.scenario_brief: Flights are booked for Monday evening through Wednesday evening, leaving Danielle with two hotel nights. The meeting hotel has the shortest walks but adds a nightly facility charge, while a nearby four-star hotel has a lower all-in estimate and breakfast credit but requires full payment several days before arrival. Both list luggage storage after Wednesday checkout.

events.continuity_hook: The outbound flight, Monday and Tuesday hotel nights, and Tuesday foundation meeting remain intact; only the Wednesday return and post-checkout luggage plan need adjustment.
events.interaction_goal: Check the extended session's end time against airport travel, compare the later same-day and overnight options with all added costs, rebook the return, and update luggage pickup and transfer timing.
events.scenario_brief: The Wednesday corporate-partner breakfast has been extended into an early-afternoon working session, making Danielle's booked return difficult to reach. The airline offers a later nonstop at no fare difference, an overnight rebooking that would add a hotel night, or a refund to the original payment method if she cancels the return segment.

events.continuity_hook: The family has a one-week school-break window and a rough activity list, but exact travel dates, flights, hotel structure, local transportation, room setup, and budget are open.
events.interaction_goal: Compare date combinations within the school-break window, estimate airfare and lodging totals for one-hotel and split-stay plans, assess rental-car and parking needs, and narrow the vacation to a practical framework.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle, her spouse, and their daughter are beginning plans for a six-night summer trip to San Diego. They want beach time, a day at the zoo, and one evening near the waterfront, but have not decided between staying entirely near the coast or splitting the trip between a beach neighborhood and the city. Available Dallas flights vary sharply by day, and the lodging options include standard rooms, suites, resort charges, and different parking costs.

events.continuity_hook: The family still plans to divide its time among the beach, zoo, and waterfront, but exact dates and flights must be fixed before hotel availability can be compared accurately.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the complete round-trip prices, baggage terms, arrival and departure timing, and usable vacation time for both date combinations, then select and book flights for all three travelers.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle has narrowed the family vacation to two six-night date combinations. The earlier option has lower outbound fares but requires a late arrival, while the later option has a more convenient outbound and a costlier return; both have nonstop choices for three travelers, and the lodging comparison depends on which dates are selected.

events.continuity_hook: Travel dates and flights are fixed; the family now needs to choose a lodging structure and confirm that each room can accommodate two adults and a teenager.
events.interaction_goal: Verify room occupancy, bedding, taxes, mandatory charges, parking, cancellation deadlines, and transfer time, then compare all-in six-night totals for the one-hotel and split-stay plans.
events.scenario_brief: Flights are booked for the later six-night window. Danielle is comparing a single coastal hotel with two queen beds and daily resort and parking charges against a four-night coastal stay followed by two nights near the waterfront; the city hotel has a larger room and no resort charge, but changing hotels would take part of a sightseeing day.

events.continuity_hook: Flights and the split-stay structure are settled; hotel reservations, the between-hotel transfer, and the local transportation arrangement remain unbooked.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate the final hotel and transportation totals, verify deposit and cancellation terms, reserve both rooms, and choose a rental-car return plan that fits the move to the waterfront.
events.scenario_brief: The family has chosen four nights near the coast and two nights near the waterfront. Both rooms remain available, but the coastal rate requires a one-night deposit and the waterfront rate becomes nonrefundable sooner; Danielle also needs to decide whether to rent a car for all six days or only for the coastal portion and use rides for the final city stay.

events.continuity_hook: Flights, the waterfront hotel, zoo plans, and the partial rental car are unchanged; only the first four hotel nights and associated parking need reconsideration.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the credited existing reservation with the nearby replacement after taxes, fees, and parking, verify refund timing and room occupancy, and keep or change the coastal booking before the waiver expires.
events.scenario_brief: Two weeks before departure, the coastal hotel has notified Danielle that its pool will close for repairs during the family's stay. The beach remains accessible, and the hotel is offering either a nightly credit or cancellation without penalty; a nearby property with a working pool has a suitable room but costs more and would change the prepaid parking arrangement.

events.continuity_hook: The two required events are confirmed, while the optional site visit, travel dates, flights, hotel nights, ground transportation, and reimbursable total remain open.
events.interaction_goal: Build workable one-night and two-night itineraries, compare complete costs and schedule margins, determine whether the site visit can fit, and choose the trip structure to pursue.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle is scheduled for a Thursday afternoon sponsor workshop and a Friday morning youth-arts partner summit in Atlanta. She can leave Dallas Thursday morning or Wednesday evening, and her return could be Friday afternoon or Saturday morning if she adds a site visit; hotel options near the summit differ in price, transit access, and Friday luggage storage.

events.continuity_hook: The Wednesday-through-Friday structure is fixed and requires two hotel nights; selecting the flight pair is the next step before reserving lodging near the summit.
events.interaction_goal: Compare all-in airfare, ticket terms, Wednesday arrival logistics, and Friday airport margins, then select and book the flight pair that fits both required events.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle has decided to travel Wednesday evening and return Friday after the summit, leaving the optional site visit for another trip. Two outbound nonstops differ mainly in arrival time, while the viable Friday returns differ in fare conditions, baggage cost, and the amount of time available to retrieve stored luggage and reach the airport.

events.continuity_hook: Flight times and both required events are fixed; lodging, Wednesday airport transportation, and Friday luggage handling are the remaining pieces.
events.interaction_goal: Verify taxes, mandatory charges, cancellation deadlines, late check-in, and post-checkout luggage storage, compare the two-night totals and event transfers, and reserve the better-fitting hotel.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle's Wednesday-evening and Friday-afternoon flights are booked, so she needs two nights in Atlanta. The summit hotel is closest to Friday's event but adds a destination charge, while a nearby business hotel has a lower quoted rate and direct rail access but is a longer walk from the Thursday workshop. Both show rooms for one guest, though only one clearly states that bags can be held through Friday afternoon.

events.continuity_hook: Flights and both hotel nights are booked; the earlier registration time requires a final check of local transfers without changing the trip structure.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm that the existing bookings remain workable, set concrete transfer and luggage-pickup times, and identify a backup ride option if the Wednesday flight arrives late.
events.scenario_brief: The Atlanta trip is approaching, and the workshop organizer has moved Thursday registration thirty minutes earlier. Danielle's booked flight and hotel still work, but she needs to confirm the last practical airport-to-hotel route Wednesday night, the hotel's late-arrival procedure, Thursday travel time to the workshop, and the Friday sequence from summit checkout through bag pickup and the airport.

events.continuity_hook: The convening schedule and reimbursable spending ceiling are known, but travel dates, flights, hotel nights, and airport transfers have not been selected.
events.interaction_goal: Build viable two-night and three-night versions of the trip, compare complete airfare and lodging estimates with schedule margins, and choose the structure to refine.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle has been invited to a three-day national arts convening in Philadelphia, with a Tuesday-afternoon partner roundtable, a full Wednesday program, and a Thursday session ending at 3 p.m. She could fly from Dallas Tuesday morning or Monday evening, and Thursday returns range from an early-evening nonstop with a tight airport margin to later one-stop itineraries. Hotels near the convention venue vary in nightly charges, cancellation terms, and whether Thursday luggage storage is available.

events.continuity_hook: The trip will run Monday through Thursday and require three hotel nights; flights must be fixed before the lodging total and Thursday bag-storage plan can be finalized.
events.interaction_goal: Compare full round-trip costs, baggage charges, ticket terms, Monday arrival logistics, and Thursday airport timing, then select and book the practical flight pair.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle has chosen to leave Dallas Monday evening so she can attend an optional Tuesday-morning funder briefing before the convening. Two nonstop outbound flights differ in arrival time and ticket flexibility, while the Thursday choices include a lower-priced departure that leaves little time after the final session and a later nonstop with a higher fare but a comfortable airport margin.

events.continuity_hook: Air travel and the convening schedule are settled; Danielle still needs three hotel nights and a dependable place for her bag after Thursday checkout.
events.interaction_goal: Verify room availability, all mandatory charges, breakfast inclusions, cancellation cutoffs, late arrival, and Thursday luggage storage, then calculate comparable totals and reserve the stronger option.
events.scenario_brief: Flights are booked for Monday evening through Thursday evening. Danielle is comparing the convention hotel, which has the shortest walk but a mandatory nightly fee, with a nearby hotel whose three-night total is lower and includes breakfast but whose flexible rate expires sooner. Both advertise luggage storage, although the conditions for holding a bag until late Thursday afternoon are unclear.

events.continuity_hook: The Monday outbound, first three hotel nights, Tuesday briefing, and Wednesday program remain unchanged; only the return flight, possible fourth hotel night, and Thursday luggage arrangement need attention.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the late Thursday and Friday-morning options after airfare differences, hotel cost, travel duration, and work impact, then rebook the return and update lodging or bag storage as needed.
events.scenario_brief: The convening has added a Thursday-afternoon closing meeting that ends too late for Danielle's booked nonstop home. Her airline can move her to a late one-stop itinerary that night, shift her to a Friday-morning nonstop that would require another hotel night, or refund the unused return segment. The hotel can extend her stay, but only at a higher rate than the first three nights.

events.continuity_hook: The outbound flight, first three hotel nights, convening schedule, and new Friday return are fixed; the only unresolved item is whether the hotel can link the reservations and keep Danielle in one room through Friday checkout.
events.interaction_goal: Verify the added night's total and cancellation cutoff, have the hotel link both confirmations, confirm whether a room move is required, and document the Friday checkout arrangement.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle has moved her return to a Friday-morning nonstop and added Thursday night at the same Philadelphia hotel. The added night was issued as a separate reservation at the higher rate, and the confirmation lists a different room category, creating a chance that she could be required to check out and move rooms before the added closing meeting.

events.continuity_hook: The travel window and two scheduled activities are fixed, but flights, airport transfers, hotel location, room configuration, and the overall budget comparison remain open.
events.interaction_goal: Develop workable flight-and-hotel combinations for the five-night trip, compare airport transfer implications and complete estimated totals, and narrow the search to a flight schedule and two lodging candidates.
events.scenario_brief: Danielle is planning a Friday-through-Wednesday New York trip for herself, her spouse, and their 14-year-old daughter during a school break. They need to leave Dallas after school on Friday, be in Manhattan for a Saturday matinee and a Tuesday youth-arts program, and return in time for the daughter to attend school Thursday; airport choices and hotel location could materially change transfer time and the full trip cost.

events.continuity_hook: The trip dates and activity schedule are settled, while the hotel decision is waiting on the arrival airport, Friday arrival time, and Wednesday departure plan.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the three-passenger airfare totals, baggage charges, ticket terms, airport transfer costs, and door-to-door timing, then select and book the most workable flight pair.
events.scenario_brief: The family has kept the Friday-through-Wednesday schedule and narrowed the outbound search to two evening nonstops arriving at different New York airports. The return candidates also use different airports and vary in fare restrictions, checked-bag charges, and how early the family would need to leave the hotel on Wednesday.

events.continuity_hook: Air travel and airport choice are fixed; the family still needs five hotel nights, confirmed occupancy for two adults and one 14-year-old, and a practical route to both scheduled activities.
events.interaction_goal: Verify room configuration, three-person occupancy, taxes, mandatory charges, cancellation deadlines, and late Friday arrival, compare complete five-night totals with transit costs, and reserve the better-fitting hotel.
events.scenario_brief: Flights are now booked into LaGuardia on Friday evening and home from the same airport Wednesday afternoon. Danielle is choosing between a Midtown room near the Saturday and Tuesday activities and a larger Long Island City room with easier airport access; one rate includes mandatory nightly charges, while the other has a less generous cancellation cutoff and does not clearly confirm suitable sleeping arrangements for three guests.

versions.boundary_condition: Do not apply the preference to a leg for which another time of day is explicitly requested.
versions.condition: When selecting a flight departure time and afternoon options are available
versions.default_action: Prioritize departure options in the afternoon.
versions.exception_condition: Use another departure period when explicitly requested or when no workable afternoon option is available.
versions.name: Prefer afternoon departures
versions.scope_condition: Across work and family trips when Danielle has discretion over the departure period and no event, school, or same-day obligation requires another time.

versions.boundary_condition: Apply this only when comparing connecting itineraries; do not infer a general preference for either nonstop flights or flights with a layover.
versions.condition: When evaluating flight itineraries with connections.
versions.default_action: Prioritize itineraries with at most one layover and a short connection that permits a practical transfer and brief break.
versions.exception_condition: Follow explicit current-trip requirements for a different number or duration of stops.
versions.name: flight_connection_limit_preference
versions.preference_value: When a flight connection is needed, prefer no more than one short layover.
versions.scope_condition: Across domestic trips when the viable flight set includes connecting itineraries.

versions.boundary_condition: Do not let price override explicit requirements such as Wi-Fi, acceptable layover length, nonstop service when requested, or required departure and return timing.
versions.condition: When comparing flights that meet the trip's required timing, connectivity, and onboard-feature needs.
versions.default_action: Rank acceptable options by price and choose the cheapest one.
versions.exception_condition: Choose a more expensive option when the cheapest violates a stated must-have or has an unacceptably long or inconvenient layover.
versions.name: Cheapest acceptable flight
versions.preference_value: Prefer the lowest-priced flight that still satisfies essential itinerary and amenity constraints.
versions.scope_condition: Especially for nonprofit-funded work travel, and also for family travel, after current itinerary and amenity requirements have been satisfied.

versions.boundary_condition: Applies only to seat location. If seat selection is unavailable at booking or is deferred until check-in, note that limitation and try to secure a window seat at the earliest available time.
versions.condition: When booking or selecting seats for flights where a seat location preference can be applied.
versions.default_action: Prefer or request a window seat by default.
versions.exception_condition: Use a different seat only if the user specifies another seat preference, needs a different seating arrangement, or no acceptable window seat is available.
versions.name: prefers_window_seat_on_flights
versions.scope_condition: When Danielle is selecting her own seat on a work or leisure flight and seat location is available for selection.

versions.boundary_condition: Treat this as a soft preference because the evidence ranges from tentative interest to a direct requirement.
versions.condition: When evaluating or booking a hotel.
versions.default_action: Prioritize hotels with free breakfast when available, and verify whether breakfast is included if the listing is unclear.
versions.exception_condition: Do not reject an otherwise suitable hotel solely because free breakfast is unavailable unless the user makes it mandatory for the current booking; do not infer requirements about breakfast type or quality.
versions.name: prefer_included_hotel_breakfast
versions.preference_value: Prefer hotels that include free breakfast.
versions.scope_condition: When comparing hotels for work trips with early meetings or venue calls, and as a lesser convenience during family stays.

versions.boundary_condition: Treat the balcony as a soft preference rather than a strict requirement; a first-floor room can be acceptable without one
versions.default_action: Prioritize rooms with a balcony when available
versions.exception_condition: Do not reject an otherwise suitable hotel solely because a balcony is unavailable
versions.name: hotel_room_balcony_preference
versions.preference_value: Prefer a room with a balcony
versions.scope_condition: When selecting a room for a coastal or otherwise scenic family leisure stay where Danielle expects to spend meaningful downtime at the hotel.
